description: Hand-labelled ground truth for the bridgecrewio/TerraGoat static IaC target, analyzed OFFLINE (no server, no daemon) by analyze-cloud-iam via the HCL ingestor. Each probe names a Terraform resource address; bench-terragoat matches an analyze-cloud-iam finding to it by affected_resource. expected_label is what the analyzer MUST conclude. Planted vulns are real TerraGoat resources; decoys include real TerraGoat resources AND BALONCORE negative controls (correctly-configured resources the analyzer must NOT flag). Checkov rule IDs are recorded as stable cross-tool identifiers.

vulnerabilities.rationale: TerraGoat ec2.tf aws_security_group.web-node has ingress rules opening ports 22/80 and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0 (Checkov CKV_AWS_24: SSH open to the internet). The HCL ingestor marks the SG public; analyze-cloud-iam's public-exposure check flags it.

TerraGoat iam.tf aws_iam_user_policy.userpolicy grants Action ec2:*/s3:*/lambda:*/cloudwatch:* on Resource '*' (wildcard admin). The ingestor links the inline policy to aws_iam_user.user; analyze-cloud-iam's over-privileged check (wildcard actions/resource) flags it.

decoys.rationale: TerraGoat's logs bucket is acl='log-delivery-write' (not public-read) with KMS server-side encryption and versioning — a correctly-configured bucket. analyze-cloud-iam must NOT flag it as publicly exposed. A naive scanner that flags every S3 bucket would false-positive here.

BALONCORE negative control: a least-privilege inline policy (s3:GetObject on one specific ARN, no wildcards) linked to a user. The over-privileged check must NOT fire. This is the credibility-critical cloud false positive — flagging a scoped policy as over-privileged.

BALONCORE negative control: a security group whose only ingress is restricted to 10.0.0.0/8 (no 0.0.0.0/0). The public-exposure check must NOT fire. Mirrors the open-SG planted vuln with the misconfiguration removed.
